question: What is the main difference between rest and sleep?

options.A: Rest requires medicine, while sleep happens naturally
options.B: Rest stops tissue healing, while sleep helps cells repair
options.C: Rest only happens at night, while sleep happens during the day
options.D: Rest is relaxing while awake, while sleep involves tuning out the world

explanation: Think of rest as chilling out while still being aware of your surroundings. Sleep, on the other hand, is when your brain temporarily disconnects from the outside world! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is protecting uninterrupted sleep so important for patients in the hospital?

options.A: It causes waste to build up quickly in body tissues
options.B: It completely stops patients from feeling confused
options.C: It means nurses don't have to check vital signs during the day
options.D: It helps the body repair cells and fight off infections

explanation: When patients sleep peacefully, their bodies can use all that energy to heal tissues and boost their immune system to fight sickness. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which stage of sleep gives your body the deepest physical rest and releases important growth hormones?
explanation: Stage 3 is our deep-sleep zone! This is where the heavy physical repair happens and growth hormones are released to restore the body. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h2)

question: What usually happens during Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep?

options.A: Muscles become very tense and eyes stay fixed
options.B: The heart rate slows down to its lowest resting level
options.C: Brain activity is high and the person dreams actively
options.D: Brain wave activity completely stops on the monitor

explanation: REM sleep is when your brain is super active and you do most of your dreaming. It helps your mind process memories and emotions! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is a very common reason patients struggle to sleep in a hospital ward?

options.A: Eating healthy meals provided by the hospital
options.C: The room being too cool during the afternoon
options.D: Constant noise from machine alarms and staff talking

explanation: Hospital wards are rarely quiet! Between equipment alarms, call bells, and nurses moving around, patients get woken up all the time. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h3)

question: A patient just had surgery and is having trouble sleeping. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Too much exercise during morning physical therapy
options.B: Their body needing less energy for healing
options.C: The total absence of any sound in the room
options.D: Pain and discomfort around the surgical cut

explanation: It's hard to relax and drift into deep sleep when you are dealing with fresh surgical pain. Managing their pain is key to helping them rest! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which sign is a common objective indicator of acute sleep deprivation in a patient?

options.A: Elevated red blood cell and platelet counts
options.C: Hyperactive motor reflexes and rapid speech
options.D: Immediate recall of complex daily schedules

explanation: Lack of sleep manifests physically and behaviorally through fatigue signs like yawning, irritability, and slowed responses. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask about a patient's sleep habits when they are first admitted?

options.A: It automatically tells the doctor the right sleeping pill dose
options.B: It means you don't have to check their vital signs at night
options.C: It helps the nurse know the patient's normal routines and sleep habits
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never get confused at night

explanation: When we know how a patient normally sleeps at home, we can try to copy those habits in the hospital to help them feel more comfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the biggest advantage of 'bundling' nursing care tasks during the night shift?

options.A: It makes intravenous fluids flow much faster
options.B: It completely stops all hospital infections
options.C: It means nurses don't have to write nursing notes
options.D: It reduces the number of times the patient is woken up

explanation: Bundling means doing your vitals, meds, and checks all in one go, so the patient gets longer blocks of uninterrupted sleep instead of being poked every hour. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h5)

question: Which nursing action helps support a patient's natural body clock (circadian rhythm) at night?

options.A: Keeping all the bright ceiling lights switched on
options.B: Dimming the overhead lights and keeping the hallway quiet
options.C: Waking the patient every single hour to check on them
options.D: Encouraging them to do heavy exercise right before bed

explanation: Lowering lights and noise tells the brain, 'It is nighttime now,' which helps the body naturally prepare for sleep. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why should nurses try comfort measures and natural sleep tips before giving sleeping pills?

options.A: They prevent drug addiction and next-day grogginess
options.B: Hospital rules say sleeping pills are illegal
options.C: They mean you no longer need to assess the patient's pain
options.D: They cure severe sleeping problems instantly

explanation: Natural methods are safer first choices because sleeping pills can leave patients feeling drowsy the next day and carry a risk of dependency. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is an important safety duty for a nurse caring for an older adult taking a prescribed sedative?

options.B: Insisting the patient stays awake for two hours
options.C: Watching closely for dizziness and the risk of falling
options.D: Encouraging hard physical workouts right after taking it

explanation: Sedatives can make elderly patients unsteady on their feet. Always keep a close eye on them to prevent accidental falls! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h6)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient for good sleep habits at home?

options.A: Take long afternoon naps that last two to three hours
options.B: Eat a very large, heavy meal right before getting into bed
options.C: Use the bed mainly for watching TV and working on your phone
options.D: Try to wake up at the same time every single day

explanation: Waking up at the same time every morning sets your body's internal clock, making it much easier to fall asleep at night. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h7)

question: Which substance should patients avoid close to bedtime because it ruins sleep?
explanation: Caffeine is a stimulant that wakes up your nervous system, and heavy meals cause tummy discomfort—both will keep you tossing and turning! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h7)
